title: Seven Goals, Seven Scorers: India Tear Pakistan Apart in London
excerpt: India produced a second-half masterclass at Lee Valley, hammering Pakistan 7-1 in the FIH Pro League to complete a memorable double and extend a decade-long unbeaten run against their arch-rivals.
body:
India's men's hockey team produced one of their most dominant performances of the season, demolishing Pakistan 7-1 in the reverse fixture of the FIH Pro League at the Lee Valley Hockey and Tennis Centre in London on Friday. Seven different players found the net as Craig Fulton's side turned a 0-1 deficit into a rout, completing a double over Pakistan after a 4-3 win earlier in the week.

## A Rocky Start, Then Total Control

Pakistan struck first through captain Abu Bakar Mahmood's drag-flick from a penalty corner in the 13th minute — his second goal against India in three days. For the rest of the match, though, it was all India.

The turning point came in the 18th minute when Pakistan forward Ahmad Nadeem was accidentally struck on the face by a deflected pass from teammate Ali Ghazanfar. Nadeem left the field in a wheelchair, visibly in pain, and his absence disrupted Pakistan's already brittle defensive shape.

India capitalised immediately. Skipper Harmanpreet Singh's powerful drag-flick was deflected in by Sukhjeet Singh in the 20th minute to level the score. Six minutes later, Harmanpreet smashed another penalty corner into the top-left corner himself. India led 2-1 at halftime, and the floodgates were about to open.

## The Second Half: A Demolition

The third quarter was devastating. Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke in the 34th minute after India earned consecutive corners. Barely 60 seconds later, Jugraj Singh finished off a stunning counter-attack — Dilpreet Singh finding Sukhjeet, who set up Jugraj for a thunderous finish to make it 4-1.

Abhishek scored on the run in the 41st minute after a creative Sukhjeet assist, and Raj Kumar Pal pounced on a rebound from Harmanpreet's drag-flick in the 44th minute to extend the lead to 6-1. Dilpreet then capped the rout in the 54th minute with India's seventh, finishing off a flowing team move.

Pakistan earned penalty corners in the dying minutes, but veteran midfielder Manpreet Singh stood firm to block both attempts.

## What It Means

The 7-1 scoreline — with seven different scorers — is a statement of India's depth and attacking variety. Combined with Tuesday's 4-3 victory, India have scored 11 goals across two matches against Pakistan in the London leg. India now sit seventh on the Pro League table with four wins this season. Pakistan remain winless in 15 matches and rooted to the bottom.

India have now been unbeaten against Pakistan for over a decade in international hockey.

## Why NRIs Should Care

For the Indian diaspora in the UK, this was a match that could be watched live at the Lee Valley centre in London — one of the rare chances to see India play on British soil. The commanding double over Pakistan reaffirms India's status as a top-tier hockey nation and gives fans in the UK a moment of genuine sporting pride. With two more matches against England still to come in the London leg, there are more opportunities to see the Indian flag in action at one of the world's premier hockey venues.

*Sources: FIH, Hockey India, Revsportz, The Indian Express*
